dialogue.scene: Grandpa's falconry trophy has disappeared from its glass cabinet during a family gathering. His granddaughters, Reem and Noura, try to work out what happened.

p1.t: The trophy was here this morning. Someone must have taken it during lunch.
Let's not jump to conclusions. Maybe one of the adults moved it. But let's go all out to find it.
Look, there's a clue: a piece of blue ribbon on the floor.
Blue ribbon? That rings a bell. Aunt Huda had ribbons like that on her gift boxes.

p2.t: So it can't be a thief. It must be Aunt Huda. She's planning a surprise for Grandpa.
She might be cleaning it for his party tonight.
Yes! I put two and two together. She's the only one with the key.
There's no doubt about it. Let's ask her and figure out the whole story.

dialogue.focus: So it can't be a thief. It must be Aunt Huda.
qs: What clue did Reem find?

dialogue.scene: Omar can't find his phone, and his family is leaving for his grandmother's house in ten minutes. His sister Lama helps him.

dialogue.scene: Sam and Faisal are recording a video show called 'The Prediction Show' for a kids' science channel. They rate how sure they are about the future.

p1.t: Welcome to The Prediction Show! First prediction: flying taxis in Riyadh by 2035.

Really? I think it's a long shot. They might be too expensive for most people.
Odds are the prices will come down. Phones were expensive once, too.

dialogue.scene: Omar and his family are visiting a date farm and factory in Qassim during the date season. The farm manager, Mr Saleh, explains the process.

p1.t: How do the dates get from the palm trees to the shops?
First of all, they're picked by hand when they're ripe, usually in late summer.
By hand? That must take ages!
It does. Then they're taken to the factory, where they're washed and dried.

p2.t: What happens to them at the factory?
After that, they're sorted out by size. Every batch goes through quality control.
And then they're packed?
Exactly. Finally, the boxes are shipped all over the world. Some end up in Japan!

dialogue.focus: First of all, they're picked by hand when they're ripe, usually in late summer.
qs: What happens to the dates when they arrive at the factory?
Where do some of the dates end up?

speakout.scene: You are a guide at a date festival. A group of tourists asks you how dates get from the farm to their table. Explain the process.

prompts.q: How are the dates collected from the trees?
prompts.hint: Use the passive: 'They are picked …' and say when.

prompts.q: What happens to them after they leave the farm?
prompts.hint: Give two steps with 'Then …' and 'After that, they are …'.

prompts.q: How do they reach other countries?
prompts.hint: Use 'Finally, they are …' and 'they end up in …'.

The Buraidah Date Festival in Qassim is one of the biggest date markets in the world.

Why do you think dates are so important in Saudi culture?

dialogue.scene: Faisal's grandfather has a new smart TV and doesn't know how to set it up. Faisal is explaining on the phone.

p1.t: Faisal, the new TV is here, but I can't set it up.
Don't worry, Grandpa. We'll do it step by step. First, plug in the TV and press the red button on the remote.
OK, the screen is on. It's asking me something in English.
Just follow the instructions. Choose Arabic, and then press OK.

p2.t: Done. Now it wants a password.
That's the Wi-Fi password. It's written on the back of the router. Make sure you type capital letters correctly.
It's connected! What next?
Once that's done, the TV updates itself. Then it'll be up and running. You'll get the hang of it, I promise!

dialogue.focus: First, plug in the TV and press the red button on the remote.
qs: Where is the Wi-Fi password written?
What happens after the TV is connected to the Wi-Fi?

speakout.scene: Your aunt has just bought her first smartphone and wants to video-call her family. Give her clear instructions.

prompts.q: The phone is still in the box. What do I do first?

prompts.q: And how do I make a video call?
prompts.hint: Use 'Once that's done, …' and 'Finally, …'.

culture.title: Around the world: Instruction manuals
points: In the past, every device came with a thick paper manual in many languages.
Today, most instructions appear on the screen or in short online videos.
Some companies use only pictures in their instructions so anyone can understand them.
qs: Do you prefer instructions in pictures, videos or words? Why?
Who do you usually help with technology in your family?

expressions.def: to remove unwanted things by passing through a filter

expressions.frame: Water is pumped from ___ to ___.

dialogue.scene: Noura is visiting her uncle Majed, an engineer at a desalination plant in Jubail. She wants to know how the plant works.

p1.t: Uncle Majed, how is seawater turned into water we can drink?
First of all, seawater is pumped from the Gulf into the plant.
Is it clean when it arrives?
Not at all. Next, sand, dirt and tiny sea creatures are filtered out.

p2.t: And how do you get rid of the salt?
The water is pushed through very fine filters, and the salt is left behind. After that, minerals are added.
So then it's ready to drink?
Almost. It's tested, then stored in huge tanks and pumped to cities on a large scale. Clever, isn't it?

dialogue.focus: First of all, seawater is pumped from the Gulf into the plant.
qs: What is filtered out of the seawater first?
What happens to the water after it is tested?

speakout.scene: You are a young guide at a science museum. A visitor asks you how seawater becomes drinking water.

prompts.q: Where does the water come from, and how does it get to the plant?
prompts.hint: Use the passive: 'Seawater is pumped …'.

prompts.q: How is the water cleaned?
prompts.hint: Give two steps with 'Next, …' and 'filtered out' or 'get rid of'.

prompts.q: How does the water finally reach our homes?
prompts.hint: Use 'After that, …' and 'Finally, it is …'.

culture.title: Around Saudi Arabia: Water from the sea
points: Saudi Arabia is one of the world's largest producers of desalinated water.
Most drinking water in cities like Riyadh comes from the sea, hundreds of kilometres away.
Engineers are now using solar energy to make the process cleaner.
qs: Why do you think saving water is so important in Saudi Arabia?
What are two easy ways your family could use less water?

3-3.exit: Explain in two sentences how seawater becomes drinking water, using 'first' and 'then'.

expressions.def: to put something in the rubbish because you don't want it

expressions.def: to make something into smaller pieces
expressions.frame: In a recycling plant, ___ are broken down into ___.

expressions.def: to use an old thing again in a new way
expressions.frame: You can give old ___ a second life by ___.

expressions.def: to put things into different groups
expressions.frame: At home, we separate ___ from ___.

expressions.frame: Eventually, the old ___ is turned into ___.

expressions.frame: ___ is melted down and used to make ___.

dialogue.scene: Sara and Lama are filming a short video for a city recycling competition. They are explaining how plastic bottles are recycled.

p1.t: So, what happens after we throw away a plastic bottle in the recycling bin?
First, the bottles are collected by trucks and taken to a recycling plant.
Are they all mixed with other rubbish?
Yes, so they're separated from paper and metal. Then they're washed.

p2.t: And after they're washed?
They're broken down into tiny pieces, and the pieces are melted down.
What do they turn into?
Eventually, they're made into new things, like T-shirts or benches. It gives plastic a second life!

dialogue.focus: First, the bottles are collected by trucks and taken to a recycling plant.
qs: Why are the bottles separated at the plant?
What can old bottles eventually turn into?

speakout.scene: Your little sister asks you why she shouldn't throw plastic bottles into the normal rubbish bin. Explain how recycling works and persuade her to recycle.

prompts.q: Where do bottles go after the recycling bin?
prompts.hint: Use the passive: 'They are collected and taken to …'.

prompts.q: What happens to them at the plant?
prompts.hint: Give two or three steps with 'Then …', 'After that …' and 'broken down'.

prompts.q: Why should I bother recycling?
prompts.hint: Use 'It's worth …' or 'You really should …' and say what they become.

culture.title: Around the world: Recycling champions
points: Germany recycles more than half of all its rubbish.
In some countries, you get money back when you return empty bottles to a machine.
Saudi Arabia plans to recycle much more of its waste as part of Vision 2030.
qs: Do you think people should get money for recycling? Why or why not?
What could your neighbourhood do to recycle more?

3-4.exit: Explain in two sentences what happens to a plastic bottle after you recycle it.

3-5.warmup: What is something you know how to do really well?

expressions.def: in a few words; as a short summary

expressions.def: to explain something to someone slowly, step by step
expressions.frame: Let me walk you through how to ___.

expressions.def: used to start explaining a process

expressions.def: the final point, but still important
expressions.frame: Last but not least, ___.

expressions.def: to understand the main idea

expressions.def: it is not as difficult as people think
expressions.frame: Making ___ is easier than it sounds.

dialogue.scene: Omar is filming a one-minute 'Explain It Like an Expert' video for a kids' cooking competition. His neighbour Ms Emma, who is from London, asks questions as he cooks.

p1.t: Today I'll walk you through how kabsa is made. In a nutshell, it's rice cooked with meat and spices.
The first step is to fry onions and tomatoes. Then the chicken is added and cooked with spices.
Which spices are used?
Usually cardamom, black lemon and cinnamon. After that, water is added and brought to the boil.

p2.t: I think I get the gist. When is the rice put in?
Once the chicken is cooked, it's taken out, and the rice is added to the soup and left to simmer.
And how is it served?
Last but not least, the rice is put on a big tray with the chicken on top. Honestly, it's easier than it sounds!

dialogue.focus: The first step is to fry onions and tomatoes. Then the chicken is added and cooked with spices.
qs: Which spices are used in Omar's kabsa?
What happens once the chicken is cooked?

speakout.scene: It's your turn in the 'Explain It Like an Expert' challenge. Choose a process you know well (a recipe, a game, a science experiment or a craft) and explain it to the judges.

prompts.q: What are you going to explain, and what is it in a nutshell?
prompts.hint: Name the process and give a one-sentence summary with 'In a nutshell, …'.

prompts.q: Walk us through the main steps.
prompts.hint: Give three or four steps with 'The first step is …', 'Then …', 'Once …' and the passive.

prompts.q: What is the last step, and do you have a tip for us?
prompts.hint: Use 'Last but not least, …' and a tip with 'Make sure …'.

culture.title: Around the world: How-to videos
points: How-to videos are some of the most popular videos on the internet.
Good explainers show each step clearly and speak slowly.
Many young Saudis share videos explaining cooking, gaming and science online.
qs: What is the best how-to video you have ever watched? What made it good?
If you made a how-to video, what would it be about?

3-5.exit: Explain a simple process to me in two sentences, using one sequencing word and one passive verb.

words.ex: Al Hilal came out on top after a very tough match.
With their best players back, the home team holds all the aces.

words.w: give someone a run for their money
words.ex: The new team gave the champions a run for their money.
Both teams went all out in the final ten minutes.
Winning the cup was a real triumph for the young players.
Brazil were the firm favourites, but they lost in the semi-final.

dialogue.t: So, who do you think will come out on top tonight?
I'm positive that Al Nassr will win. They hold all the aces this year.
Really? Their best defender is injured, so they can't be that confident.
True, but they're still the firm favourite. Everyone says so.
Al Ittihad might surprise everyone. They always give the big teams a run for their money.
They could score first, I suppose. But they can't beat Al Nassr at home.
We'll see. Both teams will go all out, that's for sure.
Whoever wins, it'll be a triumph for Saudi football. Let's watch it together!

grammar.title: Certainty and possibility about the future
grammar.ar: نستخدم I'm positive / will للتأكد التام، و might / could للاحتمال، و can't للاستحالة.
examples: I'm positive that they will win.
They might score in the first half.
They can't lose with such a strong team.

words.ex: She saw the empty box and put two and two together.
Don't jump to conclusions. Let's check the camera first.
The muddy footprints were the first clue.
It took us an hour to figure out who had the key.
Someone moved the trophy. There's no doubt about it.
Does the name 'Mr Kareem' ring a bell?

dialogue.t: The trophy was here this morning. Someone must have taken it during lunch.
Let's not jump to conclusions. Maybe one of the adults moved it. But let's go all out to find it.
Look, there's a clue: a piece of blue ribbon on the floor.
Blue ribbon? That rings a bell. Aunt Huda had ribbons like that on her gift boxes.
So it can't be a thief. It must be Aunt Huda. She's planning a surprise for Grandpa.
Yes! I put two and two together. She's the only one with the key.
There's no doubt about it. Let's ask her and figure out the whole story.

grammar.title: must / might / can't for deduction
grammar.ar: must = متأكد أنه صحيح، might/could = ممكن، can't = متأكد أنه غير صحيح. وبعدها الفعل في صيغته الأساسية.
examples: It must be the sports teacher.
She might be in the office.
It can't be a thief; the door was locked.

words.ex: There's a good chance of rain in Abha tomorrow.
Chances are the roads will be busy on Thursday night.

words.w: to be on the safe side
words.ex: To be on the safe side, take a warm jacket.
Dad keeps an eye on the weather app all day.
They called off the desert trip because of the sandstorm.
Snow is very unlikely in Jeddah.

dialogue.t: Have you checked the weather for Friday? I really want to go camping.
There's a good chance of strong wind in the afternoon.
Strong wind? It might turn into a sandstorm.
It's possible, but it's unlikely to last long. Chances are it'll calm down by evening.
I hope we don't have to call off the trip again.
I'm fairly sure we won't. But to be on the safe side, let's leave after sunset.
Good idea. I'll keep an eye on the weather app tomorrow.
And we'll go all out to make it the best camping trip ever!

grammar.title: Talking about probability
grammar.ar: نعبّر عن درجة الاحتمال: there's a good chance / chances are (مرجّح)، might (ممكن)، unlikely / I doubt (غير مرجّح).
examples: There's a good chance of rain tomorrow.
Chances are the wind will stop by evening.
It's unlikely to snow in Riyadh.

words.ex: Mum turned the house upside down looking for her keys.
Let's retrace our steps to the car park.
We looked high and low, but the ticket was gone.
Your watch is bound to turn up somewhere at home.
I must have misplaced my glasses again.
Out of the blue, my phone started ringing under the sofa.

dialogue.t: I've turned the place upside down, but I can't find my phone anywhere!
Calm down, you've just misplaced it. Let's retrace your steps. Where did you use it last?
In the kitchen, I think. But I looked high and low in there.
Then it can't be in the kitchen. It might be in the car.
No, it can't be in the car. Dad took the car to work.
Hmm. You were playing on the sofa after lunch. It must be under a cushion.
I doubt it, but OK. Wait, it's ringing! Out of the blue, Grandma's calling me!
See? It was under the cushion! I told you it was bound to turn up.

grammar.title: could / must / can't for location guesses
grammar.ar: نستخدم could / might للمكان المحتمل، must للمكان شبه المؤكد، can't للمكان المستحيل.
examples: It could be in your bag.
It must be under the sofa.
It can't be in the car; Dad has the car.

words.ex: I had butterflies in my stomach before my maths results.
Relax, an A in science is in the bag.
Noura passed her English exam with flying colours.
Keep your fingers crossed for me tomorrow!
I'm doubtful about the last question. I think I got it wrong.
I'm fairly sure I answered every question.

dialogue.t: The results come out at ten. I've got butterflies in my stomach!
Me too. I'm fairly sure I did well in science, but I'm doubtful about maths.
You studied so hard. You must have passed maths.
I'm not so sure. I couldn't figure out the last two questions.
Well, English is in the bag for you. You always get top marks.
Thanks! I doubt I got full marks, though. The essay was tricky.
Let's keep our fingers crossed. Oh, look, the results are online!
I passed maths with flying colours! I can't believe it!

grammar.title: Degrees of certainty
grammar.ar: رتّب درجات اليقين: I'm positive (متأكد جداً) > I'm fairly sure (متأكد إلى حد ما) > I doubt that (أشك).
examples: I'm positive that I passed science.
I'm fairly sure I did well.
I doubt that I got full marks.

words.w: without a shadow of a doubt
words.ex: Without a shadow of a doubt, cars will drive themselves one day.
It's a long shot, but our school might win the national prize.
Odds are we'll all have robot helpers at home.
It's a safe bet that football will still be popular.
There's no way people will stop using phones.
We take fast internet for granted today.

dialogue.t: Welcome to The Prediction Show! First prediction: flying taxis in Riyadh by 2035.
Without a shadow of a doubt! They're already testing them, so it must happen soon.
Really? I think it's a long shot. They might be too expensive for most people.
Odds are the prices will come down. Phones were expensive once, too.
Next: will families go on holiday to the Moon by 2050?
There's no way ordinary families will go to the Moon by then. It's far too expensive.

grammar.title: Rating predictions
grammar.ar: نرتّب التوقعات حسب درجة اليقين: without a shadow of a doubt / a safe bet (مؤكد)، odds are (مرجّح)، a long shot (ضعيف)، there's no way (مستحيل).
examples: It's a safe bet that tourism will grow.
It's a long shot, but we might live on Mars.
There's no way schools will disappear.

words.ex: The old town of Al-Balad is well worth a visit.
The rocks of AlUla will take your breath away.
We found a quiet village off the beaten track.
Get up early to make the most of your day.
A balloon ride over AlUla is a once-in-a-lifetime experience.
Hegra is a must-see for every visitor.

dialogue.t: We've got a week off in January. Where should we go?
If you ask me, you really should visit AlUla. It's well worth a visit.
What's so special about it?
The rocks and old tombs at Hegra will take your breath away. It's a must-see.
Is it very crowded in winter?
The main sites can be busy, but there are quiet valleys off the beaten track.
That sounds amazing. What else is worth doing?
Try a hot-air balloon ride at sunrise. It's a once-in-a-lifetime experience. Make the most of it!

grammar.title: It's worth + -ing / worth a visit
grammar.ar: بعد worth نستخدم اسماً أو فعلاً بإضافة ing: It's worth visiting. ونستخدم You really should + الفعل للتوصية القوية.
examples: It's well worth a visit.
It's worth getting up early.
You really should see Hegra.

words.ex: That mystery novel is a real page-turner.
I started it at nine and couldn't put it down.
The ending is absolutely gripping.
You've never read fantasy? Give it a go!
You love space, so this series is right up your street.
I got hooked after the first episode.

dialogue.t: I'm so bored. I've finished all my books.
You really should read 'The Desert Code'. It's a real page-turner.
What's it about? I don't usually like long books.
A boy solves a mystery in an old fort in Najran. It's right up your street, since you love mysteries.
Hmm. Is it worth reading if I don't like history?
Definitely. It's not boring at all. The ending is really gripping.
OK, I'll give it a go.
Trust me, you'll get hooked. I couldn't put it down. It'll take your breath away!

grammar.title: Persuading with reasons
grammar.ar: للإقناع نعطي توصية ثم سبباً: You really should … because … / It's worth reading because … / If you ask me, …
examples: You really should read it because the ending is gripping.
It's worth watching even if you don't like history.
If you ask me, it's the best series this year.

words.ex: My grandmother's kabsa is out of this world.
They serve mouth-watering grilled chicken.
After the long walk, that fresh juice really hit the spot.
At Boulevard, you're spoilt for choice with restaurants.
The meal wasn't cheap, but it was worth every riyal.
Let's try out that new Yemeni restaurant.

dialogue.t: There are so many restaurants here. I don't know where to go.
We're spoilt for choice! If you ask me, we should go to the Turkish place by the fountain.
Why that one? It looks expensive.
It is, but it's worth every riyal. Their mixed grill is out of this world.
I'd rather try out something new. What about that Korean stall?
Their noodles smell mouth-watering, I admit. But you really have to try the Turkish dessert.
All right, you've persuaded me. Dinner there, then Korean ice cream later.
Perfect! After all this walking, a big meal will really hit the spot.

grammar.title: Strong recommendations
grammar.ar: للتوصية القوية: You have to try … / You really should … / It's worth trying … وللرأي: If you ask me, …
examples: You have to try their mixed grill.
It's worth trying the Korean noodles.
If you ask me, it's the best restaurant in town.

words.ex: Swimming helped me get into shape.
You've never done karate? Give it a shot!
Running is hard at first, but stick with it.
Her hard work paid off when she won the race.
Training is tiring, but it's worth the effort.
In the holidays, my brother becomes a real couch potato.

dialogue.t: Ali, why don't you join the padel club with me? Training is on Mondays.
Padel? I'm not sporty at all. I'm a bit of a couch potato, to be honest.
That's exactly why you should come. It's the best way to get into shape.
But I'll be terrible at it. Everyone will laugh at me.
Nobody's good at first. Just give it a shot for a month.
A whole month? It sounds tiring.
It is, but it's worth the effort. If you stick with it, it'll pay off, I promise.
OK, you've talked me into it. I'll give it a go next Monday.

grammar.title: Persuading and answering worries
grammar.ar: للإقناع نقترح ونرد على المخاوف: Why don't you …? / If you stick with it, it'll … (الشرط الأول) / It's worth the effort.
examples: Why don't you give it a shot?
If you stick with it, you'll get into shape.
It's tiring, but it's worth the effort.

words.ex: This study app was a game changer for my grades.
The app is so user-friendly that my grandmother uses it.
You'll get the hang of it in a day or two.
I use a calendar app to keep track of my homework.
Online shopping saves time for busy families.
This app helped me cut down on screen time.

dialogue.t: I forgot my football boots again. The coach made me sit on the bench!
You really should download a planner app. It's worth trying, honestly.
Apps like that are always complicated. I'll never use it.
Not this one. It's really user-friendly. It helps me keep track of everything.
Does it do anything else?
It reminds you before every training session and match, and it saves so much time. It's been a game changer for me.
OK, but I'm not very good with new apps.
You'll get the hang of it in a day. Give it a shot, and stick with it for a week!

grammar.title: Recommending and promising results
grammar.ar: نوصي ثم نذكر النتيجة: It's worth downloading … / It'll help you + فعل / You'll get the hang of it.
examples: It's worth downloading this app.
It'll help you keep track of your homework.
You'll get the hang of it quickly.

words.ex: Her clear plan won the whole class over.
A free trip to the science museum? That's a no-brainer!
A trip to Jeddah gives you the best of both worlds: the sea and history.
You can't go wrong with a picnic in the park.
We talked our teacher into a class trip.
You don't have to decide now. Think it over.

dialogue.t: I want to win everyone over to my idea: a two-day trip to Jeddah.
Most people want the theme park in Riyadh. It's closer and cheaper.
But Jeddah gives us the best of both worlds: the Red Sea and the old town of Al-Balad.
That's true. The old houses in Al-Balad are well worth a visit.
Exactly. If you ask me, it's a no-brainer. We can go to a theme park any weekend.
What about the cost? Some families might not agree.
My uncle can drive us in his big van, so it won't cost families much. You can't go wrong with Jeddah.
You've almost talked me into it. Let me think it over tonight.

grammar.title: Building a persuasive talk
grammar.ar: الحديث المقنع: ابدأ بالفكرة (I'd like to suggest …)، ثم الأسباب (Firstly … Also …)، ثم الخلاصة (It's a no-brainer / Please think it over).
examples: I'd like to suggest a trip to Jeddah.
Firstly, it's cheap. Also, it's fun and educational.
It's a no-brainer, so please think it over.

words.ex: Tickets sold out in an hour, and I missed the boat.
I could kick myself for forgetting the date.

words.ar: بعد فوات الأوان / عند النظر للوراء
words.ex: In hindsight, I should have bought the tickets online.
We let the win slip through our fingers in the last minute.
If only I had checked my messages!
The trip was a golden opportunity to practise English.

dialogue.t: Did you get a photo with the player yesterday?
No, I missed the boat. He left ten minutes before I arrived.
Oh no! That was a golden opportunity. What happened?
I stayed home to finish a game. I could kick myself.
You should have left earlier. The event was all over social media.
I know. In hindsight, I could have taken the metro. It's much faster.
Never mind. It's a safe bet he'll come back next season.
If only I had left on time! I won't let a chance like that slip through my fingers again.

grammar.title: should have / could have + past participle
grammar.ar: should have + التصريف الثالث = كان يجب أن (ولم يحدث). could have + التصريف الثالث = كان بإمكاني (لكن لم أفعل).
examples: I should have left earlier.
I could have taken the metro.
If only I had checked the time!

words.w: leave things to the last minute
words.ex: I always leave my projects to the last minute.

words.ar: يذاكر بشكل مكثّف في وقت قصير
words.ex: Cramming the night before rarely works.
She fell behind in maths after being ill.
I failed the quiz and learned my lesson.
Let's go over the main points again.
I'll study extra hours to make up for lost time.

dialogue.t: You look upset. Is it the history test?
Yes, I only got six out of twenty. I left everything to the last minute.
Did you study at all?
I crammed the night before, but I couldn't remember anything. I should have started earlier.
You fell behind when you missed those classes. You could have asked your teacher for help.
I know. In hindsight, I shouldn't have been so shy.
Well, at least you've learned your lesson. Let's go over the next chapter together.
Thanks. I'll work hard to make up for this mark.

grammar.title: should have / shouldn't have
grammar.ar: shouldn't have + التصريف الثالث = ما كان يجب أن (لكنه حدث). ونستخدمها للندم أو لنقد تصرف في الماضي.
examples: I shouldn't have left it so late.
You should have asked for help.
She shouldn't have stayed up all night.

words.ex: I put my foot in it when I asked about her old school.
That was unkind. I take it back.
His joke hurt her feelings.
I'll make it up to you with your favourite dessert.
They talked for an hour to clear the air.

words.w: on the spur of the moment
words.ex: I said it on the spur of the moment.

dialogue.t: Hana, can we talk? I want to clear the air.
You laughed at my painting in front of everyone. You really hurt my feelings.
I know. I shouldn't have said it looked like a child's drawing. I take it back.
Why did you say it, then?
I said it on the spur of the moment. I really put my foot in it. I could kick myself.
You could have just told me privately if you didn't like it.
You're right. I wish I hadn't said anything. Can I make it up to you?
OK. Help me with my next painting, and we'll call it even.

grammar.title: I wish I hadn't … / I shouldn't have …
grammar.ar: I wish I had / hadn't + التصريف الثالث للتعبير عن الندم على شيء حدث في الماضي.
examples: I wish I hadn't laughed.
I shouldn't have said that.
You could have told me privately.

words.ex: He splashed out on new headphones.

words.w: burn a hole in your pocket
words.ex: That money was burning a hole in my pocket.
The cheap toy was a waste of money. It broke in a day.
I'm saving up for a new bike.
Think twice before you spend all your money.
I bought the game on impulse, and I never played it.

dialogue.t: Khalid, how much of your eidiya is left?
Only twenty riyals. The money was burning a hole in my pocket.
What did you buy?
I splashed out on a gaming chair and lots of snacks. I bought the chair on impulse.
And now you can't buy the football boots you wanted.
Exactly. I wish I had saved up for the boots. The chair was a waste of money.
You could have saved half and spent half. That's what I always did.
That was a big mistake. Next time I'll think twice before I spend anything.

grammar.title: I wish I had … (regret about money)
grammar.ar: I wish I had saved = ليتني ادّخرت (ولم أفعل). I wish I hadn't bought = ليتني لم أشترِ (لكني اشتريت).
examples: I wish I had saved my money.
I wish I hadn't bought that chair.
I should have thought twice.

words.ex: We ran out of water in the desert.
You need to plan ahead for long trips.

words.ar: كان من الممكن أن يكون أسوأ
words.ex: We got a flat tyre, but it could have been worse.
The delay was a blessing in disguise. We saw a beautiful sunset.
Look on the bright side: nobody was hurt.
Everything went wrong on the first day.

dialogue.t: So, how was the trip to the Edge of the World?
Honestly, everything went wrong. First, we ran out of fuel on the dirt road.
Oh no! You should have filled up in the last town.
I know. We could have planned ahead better. We didn't even bring enough water.
That sounds dangerous. How did you get back?
A family stopped and helped us. It could have been worse.
Well, look on the bright side. You made new friends!
True. It was a blessing in disguise. They invited us to their farm. But in hindsight, we should have checked everything first.

grammar.title: could have: other possibilities in the past
grammar.ar: could have + التصريف الثالث = كان ممكناً أن (خيار لم نختره). It could have been worse = كان من الممكن أن يكون أسوأ.
examples: We could have left earlier.
It could have been worse.
We should have brought more water.

words.ex: I learned the hard way that you should always save your work.
He turned over a new leaf and started doing homework on time.
We had a fight last year, but it's water under the bridge.

words.w: there's no use crying over spilt milk
words.ar: لا فائدة من البكاء على اللبن المسكوب
words.ex: The vase is broken. There's no use crying over spilt milk.
When I look back on that day, I laugh.
It's time to move on and focus on the next match.

dialogue.t: Emma, what's the biggest mistake you've ever made?
Last year, I didn't back up a month of baking videos, and my laptop crashed the night before I posted them.
Oh no! What did you do?
I had to film everything again. I learned the hard way. I should have saved them online.
How do you feel when you look back on it now?
I could have been angry for weeks, but there's no use crying over spilt milk.
So you moved on?
Yes, it's water under the bridge. I turned over a new leaf: now I back up everything. If only I had done it sooner!

grammar.title: Telling a regret story
grammar.ar: قصة الندم: ماذا حدث (الماضي البسيط) ← ما كان يجب فعله (should have) ← الأمنية (I wish I had) ← الدرس (I learned that …).
examples: I didn't save my project, and my laptop crashed.
Looking back, I should have backed it up.
I learned the hard way that technology can fail.

words.ex: First of all, the coffee beans are roasted.
The water is brought to the boil in a dallah.
Grandma showed me step by step.
Add the coffee and leave it to simmer for ten minutes.
In the meantime, the cardamom is crushed.
Once it's ready, the coffee is poured into small cups.

dialogue.t: That smells amazing! How is Arabic coffee made?
First of all, the green beans are roasted in a pan until they turn light brown.
Only light brown? I thought coffee was dark.
Not Saudi coffee. Then the beans are ground, and water is brought to the boil in a dallah.
And then you add the coffee?
Exactly. You leave it to simmer for about ten minutes. In the meantime, cardamom is crushed.
Is the cardamom added at the end?
Yes. Once it's added, the coffee is poured into small cups and served with dates. It's well worth trying!

grammar.title: Present passive in a process
grammar.ar: المبني للمجهول: is / are + التصريف الثالث. نستخدمه عندما يكون المهم هو العملية لا الشخص: The beans are roasted.
examples: The beans are roasted in a pan.
The water is brought to the boil.
The coffee is served with dates.

words.ex: The best dates are picked by hand.
The dates are sorted out by size and colour.
The dates go through three checks.
Bad dates are removed during quality control.
Qassim dates end up in shops around the world.
The boxes are shipped to Europe by sea.

dialogue.t: How do the dates get from the palm trees to the shops?
First of all, they're picked by hand when they're ripe, usually in late summer.
By hand? That must take ages!
It does. Then they're taken to the factory, where they're washed and dried.
What happens to them at the factory?
After that, they're sorted out by size. Every batch goes through quality control.
And then they're packed?
Exactly. Finally, the boxes are shipped all over the world. Some end up in Japan!

grammar.title: Passive with sequencing
grammar.ar: نربط مراحل العملية بكلمات الترتيب مع المبني للمجهول: First, they are picked. Then, they are washed. Finally, they are shipped.
examples: First, the dates are picked by hand.
After that, they are sorted out by size.
Finally, they are shipped abroad.

words.ex: Can you help me set up my new tablet?
First, plug in the charger.
Just follow the instructions on the screen.
Make sure the Wi-Fi is turned on.
Once that's done, choose your language.
The console was up and running in ten minutes.

dialogue.t: Faisal, the new TV is here, but I can't set it up.
Don't worry, Grandpa. We'll do it step by step. First, plug in the TV and press the red button on the remote.
OK, the screen is on. It's asking me something in English.
Just follow the instructions. Choose Arabic, and then press OK.
Done. Now it wants a password.
That's the Wi-Fi password. It's written on the back of the router. Make sure you type capital letters correctly.
It's connected! What next?
Once that's done, the TV updates itself. Then it'll be up and running. You'll get the hang of it, I promise!

grammar.title: Imperatives with sequencing
grammar.ar: للتعليمات نستخدم فعل الأمر (Plug in / Press / Choose) مع كلمات الترتيب: First … Then … Once that's done … Finally …
examples: First, plug in the TV.
Then choose your language.
Once that's done, enter the password.

words.ex: Seawater is turned into fresh water.
Sand and dirt are filtered out first.
Seawater is pumped into the plant.
Saudi Arabia produces fresh water on a large scale.
Clean water is stored in huge tanks.
Special machines get rid of the salt.

dialogue.t: Uncle Majed, how is seawater turned into water we can drink?
First of all, seawater is pumped from the Gulf into the plant.
Is it clean when it arrives?
Not at all. Next, sand, dirt and tiny sea creatures are filtered out.
And how do you get rid of the salt?
The water is pushed through very fine filters, and the salt is left behind. After that, minerals are added.
So then it's ready to drink?
Almost. It's tested, then stored in huge tanks and pumped to cities on a large scale. Clever, isn't it?

grammar.title: Passive: is / are + past participle
grammar.ar: نستخدم is مع المفرد و are مع الجمع: Water is pumped. Minerals are added. ويمكن إضافة by لذكر الفاعل إن كان مهماً.
examples: Seawater is pumped into the plant.
Sand and dirt are filtered out.
The salt is removed by special filters.

words.ex: Don't throw away that bottle. It can be recycled.
The bottles are broken down into small pieces.
Recycling gives plastic a second life.
Paper is separated from plastic.
Eventually, the pieces are made into new clothes.
The plastic is melted down and shaped again.

dialogue.t: So, what happens after we throw away a plastic bottle in the recycling bin?
First, the bottles are collected by trucks and taken to a recycling plant.
Are they all mixed with other rubbish?
Yes, so they're separated from paper and metal. Then they're washed.
And after they're washed?
They're broken down into tiny pieces, and the pieces are melted down.
What do they turn into?
Eventually, they're made into new things, like T-shirts or benches. It gives plastic a second life!

grammar.title: Passive with 'then' and 'eventually'
grammar.ar: في وصف العمليات الطويلة نستخدم: First … Then … After that … Eventually (في النهاية) مع المبني للمجهول، ويمكن حذف are الثانية: They're washed and dried.
examples: The bottles are collected and taken to a plant.
Then they're broken down into tiny pieces.
Eventually, they're made into T-shirts.

words.ex: In a nutshell, bread is made from flour, water and yeast.

The first step is to wash the rice.

dialogue.t: Today I'll walk you through how kabsa is made. In a nutshell, it's rice cooked with meat and spices.
The first step is to fry onions and tomatoes. Then the chicken is added and cooked with spices.
Which spices are used?
Usually cardamom, black lemon and cinnamon. After that, water is added and brought to the boil.
I think I get the gist. When is the rice put in?
Once the chicken is cooked, it's taken out, and the rice is added to the soup and left to simmer.
And how is it served?
Last but not least, the rice is put on a big tray with the chicken on top. Honestly, it's easier than it sounds!

grammar.title: Structuring an explanation
grammar.ar: الشرح الجيد: ملخص (In a nutshell) ← الخطوات بالترتيب (The first step is … Then … Once …) ← الخطوة الأخيرة (Last but not least) مع المبني للمجهول.
examples: In a nutshell, kabsa is rice cooked with meat and spices.
The first step is to fry the onions.
Last but not least, it is served on a big tray.
